approachQuestion.prompt: Ignore list boundaries and read all integer leaves left to right. Return the number of maximal runs of equal consecutive integers, without constructing this flattened sequence. Examples: [[2,2],[],[2,5],[5,2]] returns 3; [[],[]] returns 0; 9 returns 1.
constraints: A value is either a signed 32-bit integer or an ordered list of values; lists may be empty.
The input is finite, acyclic, and has no shared subobjects. There are n total integer and list objects, including the root, with 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000; maximum nesting depth is h ≤ 1000.
Do not modify the input. Indexing a list, reading a tag, and integer comparisons take constant time.
Return one integer. Empty regions contribute no leaves.

options.text: Subtract one for every adjacent pair of child lists, even if a child is empty or their boundary values differ.
options.feedback: [[1],[2]] has two runs and no merge is allowed.

options.text: Have each call return whether it is empty plus its first leaf, last leaf, and run count. Combine nonempty children in order, adding counts and subtracting one when the previous last leaf equals the next first leaf.
options.feedback: Only one boundary can merge when adjacent child sequences are joined; empty children do not create boundaries.

options.text: For each child boundary, rescan the already processed descendants to recover the most recent leaf, while otherwise counting runs correctly.
options.feedback: The boundary information is correct, but repeated rescans can be removed by retaining the last leaf in the summary.

options.text: Sum the run counts of all child regions without any boundary correction.

feedback.reason: Joining two nonempty summaries merges one boundary run exactly when left.last equals right.first.
details: An integer returns (nonempty,first=x,last=x,runs=1). A list folds its child summaries in order. Ignore empty summaries; when joining two nonempty summaries, add their run counts and subtract one exactly when the left last value equals the right first value. Retain the outer first and last values.

Joining two nonempty summaries merges one boundary run exactly when left.last equals right.first. Ignore empty children, which add no boundary value. Keeping only child run counts would miss cross-list merges.
“Subtract one for every adjacent pair of child lists, even if a child is empty or their boundary values differ.”: [[1],[2]] has two runs and no merge is allowed.

“Have each call return whether it is empty plus its first leaf, last leaf, and run count. Combine nonempty children in order, adding counts and subtracting one when the previous last leaf equals the next first leaf.”: Only one boundary can merge when adjacent child sequences are joined; empty children do not create boundaries.

“For each child boundary, rescan the already processed descendants to recover the most recent leaf, while otherwise counting runs correctly.”: The boundary information is correct, but repeated rescans can be removed by retaining the last leaf in the summary.
“Sum the run counts of all child regions without any boundary correction.”: [[2],[2]] is one run, not two.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n and h have the meanings in Q1. Use child indices and references without copying lists. Count active call frames; exclude input and returned output. There is no tail-call elimination. No hashing is used. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: Constant-size first/last/run summaries combine once per child.
details: Each child summary is merged once with constant work and constant state per frame. The worst input requires inspecting every object.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
